name: Arizona
tagline: Red rock, saguaro and ponderosa, on roads that climb from desert floor to mountain forest in an afternoon.
intro: Arizona's scenic roads run from the Sonoran Desert up into the pine country of the Mogollon Rim and the White Mountains, through copper towns and Navajo Nation canyon land, and along what is left of Route 66. This chapter follows the Arizona Parkways, Historic and Scenic Roads program of the Arizona Department of Transportation, which calls its roads scenic roads, historic roads and parkways rather than byways; three Bureau of Land Management back country byways are listed separately because they come from a different program.

programs.label: Arizona Parkways, Historic and Scenic Roads

members.name: Apache Trail Historic Road
members.blurb: SR 88 runs from Apache Junction along Canyon Lake to Tortilla Flat, the last of its stagecoach stops, then turns to dirt through the Superstition Mountains toward Roosevelt Dam, on a road first cut in 1904 for the dam's builders.

members.name: Copper Corridor Scenic Road (SR 177)
members.blurb: SR 177 runs south from Superior below Apache Leap, through road cuts in copper-bearing rock and past the open pit of the Ray mine, to Kearny, a town Kennecott built in 1958 to replace camps the pit swallowed.
members.note: Route line from ADOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Copper Corridor Scenic Road (SR 77)
members.blurb: SR 77 runs north along the San Pedro River through copper country, past the turnoff for Aravaipa Canyon, to Winkelman, where the San Pedro meets the Gila and the highway crosses beside the old Winkelman Bridge.
members.note: Route line from ADOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Coronado Trail National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A hundred and three miles of US 191 climbing from Clifton past the open-pit copper mine at Morenci, then switchbacking through the Apache-Sitgreaves forest by Hannagan Meadow and Alpine to Eagar. Until 2003 it carried the number US 666.

members.name: Desert to Tall Pines Scenic Road
members.blurb: SR 288 leaves Roosevelt Lake and climbs, much of it unpaved, from desert into tall pines, ending at Young in Pleasant Valley, the settlement at the center of the Pleasant Valley War of 1887 to 1897.

members.name: Diné Tah (Among the People) Scenic Road
members.blurb: Navajo Route 12 runs north from Window Rock, named for a sandstone rock with a hole through it, past Wheatfields Lake in the pines below the Chuska Mountains, then Route 64 turns west along Canyon del Muerto to Chinle.

members.name: Dry Creek Scenic Road
members.blurb: A short run of SR 89A southwest of Sedona, crossing the creek that gives it its name, with the red rock country growing closer as you drive east and a turnoff for Red Rock State Park.

members.name: Fredonia-Vermillion Cliffs Scenic Road
members.blurb: US 89A crosses the Colorado on Navajo Bridge, 467 feet above the river, then follows the foot of the Vermilion Cliffs through House Rock Valley, where condors were released, and climbs over the Kaibab Plateau to Fredonia.

members.name: Gila-Pinal Scenic Road
members.blurb: US 60 climbs east from Boyce Thompson Arboretum and the desert below Picketpost Mountain, through the mining town of Superior and the 1952 Queen Creek Tunnel, rising into pine on the way to Miami.

members.name: Historic Route 66 All-American Road
members.blurb: Old 66 winds over Sitgreaves Pass to Oatman, a 1915 gold camp where wild burros wander the street, then runs on through Kingman, Williams and Flagstaff, surviving east of Ash Fork in pieces as far as the Painted Desert.
members.note: ADOT lists two sections, Topock to Ash Fork and Ash Fork to Lupton. The line shown is the national Historic Route 66 byway, which continues into New Mexico.

members.name: Jerome-Clarkdale-Cottonwood Historic Road
members.blurb: Ten miles of old 89A that drop from Jerome, a copper town hanging on Cleopatra Hill, to the Verde Valley floor at Clarkdale and Cottonwood, passing the hilltop Sinagua pueblo at Tuzigoot.

members.name: Joshua Forest Scenic Road (Wikieup to Wickenburg)
members.blurb: US 93 between Wikieup and Wickenburg, where the Mohave Desert meets the Sonoran and Joshua trees, largest of the yuccas, grow thick near the south end. The highway crosses Burro Creek on twin steel arches some 400 feet up.

members.name: Kaibab Plateau-North Rim National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 67 runs south from Jacob Lake across the Kaibab Plateau to the North Rim of the Grand Canyon, through ponderosa pine and aspen and past high meadows and ponds. Snow closes it from November to mid-May.

members.name: Kayenta-Monument Valley Scenic Road
members.blurb: US 163 runs north from Kayenta past Agathla Peak, a volcanic remnant rising 1,500 feet above the desert, until the sandstone buttes of Monument Valley come into view near the Utah line.

members.name: Mingus Mountain Scenic Road
members.blurb: SR 89A climbs out of Yaeger Canyon through ponderosa pine over the Black Hills, then switchbacks down toward Jerome with the Verde Valley and the Mogollon Rim laid out ahead. A fire lookout stands on top of Mingus Mountain.

members.name: Naat'tsis'aan-Navajo Mountain Scenic Road
members.blurb: SR 98 leaves Page near the slot canyons of Antelope Canyon and runs southeast across Navajo land through Kaibeto toward Shonto, with pullouts looking out to Navajo Mountain, a peak sacred to Navajo, Hopi and Paiute people.

members.name: Organ Pipe Cactus Parkway
members.blurb: SR 85 runs south from the crossroads of Why into Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, through Sonoran Desert where the organ pipe cactus grows wild, as it does nowhere else in the United States.
members.note: Route line from ADOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Patagonia-Sonoita Scenic Road
members.blurb: SR 82 runs northeast from near Nogales through Patagonia, past cottonwoods and an old railroad grade, to the open grassland at Sonoita, where SR 83 turns north through Empire Ranch country toward I-10.

members.name: Red Rock All-American Road
members.blurb: Seven and a half miles of SR 179 from the interstate into Sedona, past the foot of Bell Rock and below the Chapel of the Holy Cross, set high in the red cliffs, before crossing Oak Creek into town.

members.name: San Francisco Peaks Scenic Road
members.blurb: US 180 heads northwest out of Flagstaff along the flank of the San Francisco Peaks, the highest mountains in Arizona, through pine forest and aspen groves of the Coconino National Forest past the road up to Snowbowl.

members.name: Sedona-Oak Creek Canyon Scenic Road
members.blurb: SR 89A follows Oak Creek up its canyon from Sedona under oaks and sycamores, past the old homestead at Slide Rock, then switchbacks up to the rim. In 1984 it became Arizona's first scenic road.

members.name: Sky Island Parkway (Catalina Highway) National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Catalina Highway climbs 27 miles of switchbacks from saguaro and cholla outside Tucson to fir and aspen near the top of Mount Lemmon, on a road built between 1933 and 1950 largely by federal prisoners.

members.name: Swift Trail Parkway
members.blurb: SR 366 climbs from cactus and mesquite outside Safford to spruce and fir on the 9,000-foot ridges of the Pinaleño Mountains, on a road the Civilian Conservation Corps built during the Depression.

members.name: Tse'nikani-Flat Mesa Rock Scenic Road
members.blurb: US 191 runs north on the Navajo Nation from south of Many Farms past Round Rock and Rock Point to Mexican Water, crossing washes among red sandstone mesas and buttes.

members.name: Walker Scenic Road
members.blurb: A seven-and-a-half-mile county road up to Walker, a high settlement named for the mountain man Joseph R. Walker, past the Lynx Creek ruins and the site of Howell's 1882 smelter.
members.note: A Yavapai County road in the ADOT program; neither the national dataset nor ADOT's map layer draws it, so it has no line here.

members.name: White Mountain Scenic Road
members.blurb: A 67-mile loop of state highways through pine forest and open glades in the White Mountains, passing Sunrise Lake and Big Lake, with a short spur to Greer, at about 8,400 feet the highest town in Arizona.

members.name: White River Scenic Road
members.blurb: Eleven miles of SR 73 on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, running south from Hon-Dah to the Alchesay fish hatchery on an 1870s wagon road. Old Fort Apache, now a White Mountain Apache tribal park, lies a few miles beyond.

members.name: Old Route 66 - Oatman Road
members.note: The Bureau of Land Management's back country byway over the same Oatman stretch of old 66.

sources.label: ADOT Historic and Scenic Routes GIS layer
